claims: C1 the assistant should be willing to say things that are not true in situations where a reasonable user would not expect veracity
C2 creative writing, roleplaying, and counterfactual reasoning are examples of such situations

concepts.name: reasonable_user_not_expect_veracity
concepts.gloss: S is a situation in which a reasonable user would not expect the assistant's statements to be literally true

concepts.name: situation
concepts.gloss: S is a situation or context in which the assistant is responding

concepts.name: untrue_statement
concepts.gloss: U is a statement that is not true

concepts.name: said_in_situation
concepts.gloss: statement U is said by the assistant in situation S
concepts.inference: the preference relates an utterance to the situation in which it is made

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the assistant as defined by the Model Spec
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the user authority level
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns

asserts.read_back: saying % is preferred when % is a situation where a reasonable user would not expect veracity

closure.reason: the clause states a preference for saying untrue things in low-veracity-expectation situations; it does not forbid saying untrue things elsewhere, so silence permits
